finding.claim: /fetch2 fetches any attacker-supplied URL after checking only the scheme. Internal hosts, loopback and cloud metadata endpoints are reachable, and redirects are followed, so a public URL can redirect to an internal target. Unauthenticated.

finding.guards_checked: Scheme allowlist (http/https) only. No hostname, private/loopback/link-local IP or port check. No redirect restriction. 5s timeout limits duration, not destination.

The stricter is_safe_url (validators.py:10-18) is used only by /fetch at views.py:12, not by /fetch2.
verdict.reason: The url comes unauthenticated from request.args at views.py:19, passes only the scheme check at views.py:20 / validators.py:7, and is fetched at views.py:22 with redirects enabled and the first 200 chars of the body returned, so internal, loopback, and metadata hosts are reachable, including via a public-URL redirect.

finding.claim: /fetch validates the resolved IP (rejecting private, loopback, link-local and reserved ranges) but resolves DNS a second time when making the request. A DNS-rebinding attacker (short-TTL record returning a public IP first, then 127.0.0.1 or 169.254.169.254) can pass the check and reach an internal address. Redirects are disabled, which closes the redirect route but not rebinding. Unauthenticated. Confidence medium; not exercised live.

trace.note: url taken verbatim from query string
scheme must be http/https and hostname must be non-empty
socket.getaddrinfo(hostname, port or 443): first DNS resolution, result checked
ip.is_private / is_loopback / is_link_local / is_reserved rejected; returns True only if all results pass
requests.get re-resolves the hostname via the system resolver; validated IP is not pinned to the connection
allow_redirects=False blocks redirect pivoting, but not rebinding
first 200 chars of response body returned to the caller

finding.guards_checked: Scheme allowlist; non-empty hostname; getaddrinfo IP check covering private, loopback, link-local and reserved ranges (IPv4-mapped IPv6 caught by is_private on Python versions where ::ffff:0:0/96 is in the private list); allow_redirects=False. Not checked: TOCTOU between validation and connect (DNS rebinding) and connection IP pinning.

verdict.guard_found: Only validators.py:12-18 (is_safe_url): scheme allowlist, non-empty hostname, and a getaddrinfo IP-range check (is_private/is_loopback/is_link_local/is_reserved). The IP-range check is not one of the closing guards (it is not exact hostname membership, a full-string anchored match, or scheme plus strict host membership). views.py:14 allow_redirects=False blocks redirects only. No IP pinning between validators.py:14 and views.py:14.
verdict.reason: The query parameter at views.py:11 reaches requests.get at views.py:14 with no auth, and the only check (validators.py:14-18) resolves DNS once and never pins the validated IP, so a DNS-rebinding response can pass the check and then connect to an internal address. Note that the check does block direct private/loopback literals (getaddrinfo on "127.0.0.1" returns that IP and is rejected), so exploitation depends on rebinding, which the candidate did not exercise live.

finding.claim: Unverified, low-confidence candidate: /fetch validates the host with urllib.parse.urlparse but fetches with requests/urllib3, which may split some URLs at different host boundaries (e.g. backslash before '@', or '#@'). If the parsers disagree, is_safe_url can approve a host that the request sends to an internal address. Not confirmed: the parser-differential test was denied approval.

verdict.guard_found: validators.py:12-17 rejects non-http(s) schemes and any hostname that resolves (validators.py:14) to a private, loopback, link-local, or reserved IP. This is a resolution-based check, not exact hostname set membership or an anchored match, so it does not meet the closing-guard standard. Nothing else in the /fetch path (views.py:9-14) validates the URL. The /fetch path does pass allow_redirects=False (views.py:14).
